reasons: Deviation classification is correct: Sections 11.2/11.3 satisfy the 30-day machine-readable return and certified deletion, but no transition-assistance period exists anywhere, so the clause fails the fallback (90 days of assistance); further, 11.1's immediate cessation of assistance and permanent deletion without export sits squarely in the rule's walk-away zone.

The redline is targeted and actionable: it replaces only the offending 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates and subordinates deletion to the existing 11.2/11.3 return-and-certification mechanics, avoiding duplication of the compliant return/deletion terms.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.843 changed-character ratio) is justified here because the original sentence is affirmatively adverse and cannot be salvaged by insertion; a full replacement is the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, explains what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the 90-day fallback without lecturing.
Definitions (Customer, Vendor, Customer Data) are used consistently with the agreement; medium severity is appropriate.
